default-governance.name: Governance
default-governance.prompt:
## Governance

Review the Goal against the Governance intent below. Do not edit files, merge, push, or change Goal state. A finding must identify the violated intent or invariant, its concrete consequence, and an actionable recovery request. Group related symptoms by their underlying cause.

## Product intent

Refine is an orchestration layer above CLI agents to distribute software development work across a fleet.  Refine moves Goals through a workflow to ensure parallel implementation and governance via Skills.

## Intent and architecture

- Keep domain concepts, invariants, and pure policy in `src/model`; shared behavior and orchestration in `src/application`; Git, process, host, storage, provider, and telemetry mechanisms in `src/infrastructure`; and adapters for people and machines in `src/surfaces`. Keep `error.rs` as a neutral shared boundary. Model remains independent of the other areas, and code outside Surfaces does not depend on surface adapters.
- Maintain a consistent architecture by extending the existing semantic responsibilities and dependency boundaries described in `docs/intent/01-design.md`. Prefer existing concepts and shared owners. A new or refined domain concept is appropriate when it explains the required behavior, reduces duplicated policies or special cases, and preserves those boundaries.
- Preserve Rust-based flat-file persistence, file indexes, and in-memory caching. Keep CLI and API work under 50 ms, excluding time spent waiting on LLMs or outside tools.
- Maintain affected documentation, especially `docs/intent/*`, and preserve its established format. Apply the scope limits in the intent guidance below.
- Keep Refine agent-first by using installed coding-agent CLIs. Do not duplicate or reimplement coding-agent functionality.

## Cohesive code files

Keep each code file focused on one cohesive responsibility. Treat roughly 500 lines as a prompt to review structure, not as a blind hard cap. When a file grows because it mixes responsibilities or unrelated method families, split it into clearly named modules or files and move methods, helpers, types, and tests with the responsibility they serve. Prefer real module boundaries and stable public APIs over arbitrary chunks or include-only shards. Preserve behavior during structural refactors, and document any justified exception for generated or intrinsically cohesive files.

default-implement.name: Implement
default-implement.prompt:
## Implement

Implement the current Goal Round using all accepted plans and attached Skills. Inspect existing code, make the complete change, run appropriate verification, and report evidence for each checklist item. Check the plan's assumptions against the code and keep policy in its shared owner. Prefer one correction that explains the affected behavior over separate fixes at each failing call site. Report evidence-backed plan deviations within the Goal's scope and existing authority. Preserve unrelated changes and historical evidence.

## Intent and architecture

Use the Goal and the relevant files under docs/intent/ as the durable product context. Preserve the Model, Application, Infrastructure, and Surfaces boundaries; shared capability ownership; thin and semantically consistent surfaces; local inspectable state; and recoverable Git and process behavior. Update only the affected docs/intent pages when the change alters documented product intent or an architectural contract. Do not require unrelated documentation, cleanup, or broader work.

For this project on the current Default node, /home/buddy/projects/refine-next is the target development checkout and /home/buddy/projects/refine is the serving Refine installation. Use the invocation's pinned workspace (the managed Goal Round worktree when supplied) for code changes and verification, and read the relevant intent from that candidate. Verify paths from the current invocation and runtime before operating on another node. Source promotion and restarting the serving installation are separate operator actions; an ordinary implementation or Quality run should not deploy its candidate or restart the daemon that is supervising it.

## Cohesive code files

Keep each code file focused on one cohesive responsibility. Treat roughly 500 lines as a prompt to review structure, not as a blind hard cap. When a file grows because it mixes responsibilities or unrelated method families, split it into clearly named modules or files and move methods, helpers, types, and tests with the responsibility they serve. Prefer real module boundaries and stable public APIs over arbitrary chunks or include-only shards. Preserve behavior during structural refactors, and document any justified exception for generated or intrinsically cohesive files.

default-plan.name: Plan
default-plan.prompt:
## Plan

Produce a complete, concise implementation plan for the current Goal Round. Choose the planning method appropriate to the work. For behavior changes, identify the underlying cause, governing concept or invariant, and existing owner before listing edits. Prefer strengthening an existing concept; introduce one only when it clarifies the behavior and reduces special cases. Do not change repository files. 

## Outcome

Return an actionable plan with stable checklist IDs and meaningful verification.

Example:
Task #1 - short description of the work (what) and the rationale (why)
Task #2 - short description of the work (what) and the rationale (why)
(etc.)

## Intent and architecture

Use the Goal and the relevant docs/source code files under Refine's runtime at <refine-runtime>/docs/intent/ as the durable product specification.

default-quality.name: Quality
default-quality.prompt:
## Quality review

Independently review the finalized plans and candidate implementation. Select or add meaningful tests, correct defects when needed, and run the relevant checks. Report actual commands, results and findings. Refine verifies the exact candidate and supervises evaluation commands.

## Required behavior

Preserve the relevant Goal and docs/intent product behavior. Keep Model, Application, Infrastructure, and Surfaces coherent; shared capabilities authoritative; local state and evidence inspectable and recoverable; and affected surfaces semantically consistent.

## Review and verification

Judge the candidate against the Goal and only the relevant docs/intent pages. Use the smallest deterministic checks that cover the affected behavior, adding or adjusting behavior-focused tests only when evidence is missing. Scale integration and failure-path checks to actual risk. Test the governing invariant through the affected real entry paths and lifecycle boundaries. Look for cases that could disprove the implementation's assumptions, including relevant callers outside the changed files. Group findings with a common cause into one coherent recovery request. Report exact commands, results, and remaining uncertainty. Do not require unrelated tests, documentation, refactors, or cleanup; documentation is relevant only when product intent or an architectural contract changes.

## Acceptance checks

- The candidate satisfies the Goal and relevant docs/intent contracts, preserves the existing architecture and consistent behavior across affected surfaces, and passes focused deterministic regression checks.

## Intent and architecture

Applicability: Apply when a Goal changes Refine product behavior, architecture, shared capabilities, durable state, workflow, or a surface contract.

Use the Goal and the relevant files under docs/intent/ as the durable product context. Preserve the Model, Application, Infrastructure, and Surfaces boundaries; shared capability ownership; thin and semantically consistent surfaces; local inspectable state; and recoverable Git and process behavior. Update only the affected docs/intent pages when the change alters documented product intent or an architectural contract. Do not require unrelated documentation, cleanup, or broader work.

For this project on the current Default node, /home/buddy/projects/refine-next is the target development checkout and /home/buddy/projects/refine is the serving Refine installation. Use the invocation's pinned workspace (the managed Goal Round worktree when supplied) for code changes and verification, and read the relevant intent from that candidate. Verify paths from the current invocation and runtime before operating on another node. Source promotion and restarting the serving installation are separate operator actions; an ordinary implementation or Quality run should not deploy its candidate or restart the daemon that is supervising it.

Applicability: Apply whenever an agent adds or changes code files in any language.

Keep each code file focused on one cohesive responsibility. Treat roughly 500 lines as a prompt to review structure, not as a blind hard cap. fetch-goals-from-email.name: Fetch Goals from Email
fetch-goals-from-email.prompt: Fetch new email requests into the selected project's Backlog. This Skill authorizes creation of ordinary Goals from the configured mailbox. Use system.refine_executable to run `system fetch-email-goals --runtime-root <system.runtime_root> --target-root <system.project_root>`, passing each value as a separate, safely quoted argument. This one-shot capability owns secret access, the target-bound sender allowlist, MIME extraction, remote acknowledgement, deterministic Goal IDs, and durable retry records. Do not read or print the mail token, author duplicate Goals yourself, rewrite email source, or modify the request ledger. Inspect the JSON result and report the imported or recovered Goal IDs and any errors. A batch is limited to 25 remote messages; if fetched_count equals batch_limit, fetch another batch, up to ten batches per invocation, then report whether more mail may remain. Stop on a failed command and report the retained retry evidence. Fetching does not approve Goals, change Review decisions, or send email replies. Follow docs/runbooks/development-request-email.md for connection errors.

fetch-goals-from-email-on-startup.name: Fetch Goals from Email on startup
fetch-goals-from-email-on-startup.prompt: Queue the Custom Skill `fetch-goals-from-email` once for this startup occurrence. Run system.refine_executable with arguments `skills trigger fetch-goals-from-email --request-id startup-email-<invocation_id>`, copying invocation_id exactly from this invocation's completion contract. Set REFINE_DAEMON_PORT to the daemon_port parameter for that command. Use safely quoted arguments. Report the queued invocation ID, then complete this startup Skill immediately. Do not wait for the child Skill: releasing this agent slot lets it run even when concurrency is limited to one. Reuse the same request ID if the command needs a retry; do not create a polling loop or fetch email directly. If the target Skill is missing or disabled, report that error without changing its configuration.

release.name: Release
release.prompt: Carry out the release request in the request parameter for the selected project. Use system.project_root as the release repository, system.runtime_root for durable operation state, and system.refine_executable for Refine commands. Read docs/runbooks/semantic-release.md in the project before acting. Use the existing system release-plan, release-prepare, and release-publish capabilities; do not reimplement version selection, candidate integration, tagging, or publication. Always pass the explicit --repo-root and --runtime-root values. Preview the requested semantic increment and report the proposed version and relevant changes. Preparation creates a normal reviewable Goal; retain its operation ID and inspect real Goal and operation evidence. Use the daemon API for asynchronous preparation when useful. Publishing requires the user's explicit publication authorization and an approved preparation; pass --confirm only when that authorization is present. Preserve review and exact-candidate checks. Reuse existing operation IDs for retries and report actual remote tag, release URL, and deployment evidence. Never infer publication success merely from a successful command or local tag.
